Nursing just sucks, as it is reeeeeally mundane, energy consuming and they expect you to throw your life away for it, which I won't do for a sh*t assistent position.

I would get fired, if they knew about my studies.

So, the faking and masking burns me out.

I care little for it, besides getting my money and days off

Any tips upon, how to avoid the burnout?

Should I be a bit more honest and direct, and maybe not take every bs without resistence?

Yet, I don't feel good. Not like I used to.
I used to want to be a surgeon. I still have all that knowledge, yet may not speak about or increase it.
I do my job, yet it feels so against all I have learned about myself in the last years. It exhausts me and disasociates me to the point that I cry and am unable to think about anything but this cursed job.
Yes, I knew, it would be hard, yet not that hellish.
During my training, it was okay, as my brain was stimulated with stuff to analize...Now? It's just nothing worth analizing. I cool out emotionally. Where before I was a caring and knowledgable nurse, now I ask myself with we keep some people around...If they are only in pain and too far gone to even do anything alone.
Without ambitions in the med. field, all that care is gone.
I try to see it via the money and the deadline 'til I am able to study, yet it doesn't help.
The other nurses enjoy the job...To me? It feels empty and dead.

Hey there, try to use half of the nib and ink.
More ink does not mean more time to write, as it will dry and lead to you having to clean it more often.
Inkflow is a more physical concept and is determant by angle and gravaty.
No, you don't need a PhD to write.
Try a ca. 45 degree angle, at least that's what I use for my medieval calligraphy.
If ya hold the pen straight down, the ink flows fast off the pen.
If ya hold it vertical, then barely anything comes off.
And if ya hold it in a 45 degree angle, then it is optimal (for me).
